body.p: The Chat view in AI Positron has a drop-down menu where you can choose between custom chat modes (e.g. Chat/Ask/DITA Agent). Each of these chat modes define an initial prompt and a set of tools that are used when the chat is started. Extra chat modes can be added by creating custom AI actions with a specific output-action, as exemplified below:{ "id": "my.custom.chat.mode", "title": "S1000D", "description": "Chat with the AI about your S1000D project.", "categoryId": "Chat modes", "output-action": "agentic", "prompt_ref": "prompts/s100d-detailed-prompt.md", "expand-params": [ { "name": "applicationContext", "value": "${applicationContext}" } ], "parameters": { "function_refs": [ {"ref": "get_current_document_location"}, {"ref": "get_document_content"}, {"ref": "search_project_resources"}, {"ref": "search_webhelp_content"}, {"ref": "grep_project"}, {"ref": "list_dir"}, {"ref": "copy_move_rename_path"}, {"ref": "run_command_line"}, {"ref": "edit_document"}, {"ref": "invoke_ai_action"}, {"ref": "retrieve_ai_actions"}, {"ref": "get_xml_refactoring_operations"}, {"ref": "get_xml_refactoring_operation_params"}, {"ref": "refactor_xml_with_operation"}, {"ref": "refactor_xml_with_xslt"}, {"ref": "store_to_memory"}, {"ref": "clear_memory"}, {"ref": "validate_content"} ] } }

The tools contributed by other plugins and add-ons, and the tools provided by the configured MCP servers, do not have to be listed in function_refs. They are added automatically to every chat mode. For the tools contributed by plugins and add-ons, the following exceptions apply:
A chat mode whose ID ends with .ask or contains .ask., such as the built-in Ask chat mode, is offered only the contributed tools that declare they do not change anything.
A chat mode that runs from a transformation, through the AI XPath functions, gets only the tools listed in its function_refs.
A contributed tool that replaces a built-in one is offered only in the chat modes that list the built-in tool.

section.title: Defining a Sub-Agent in a Markdown File
section.p: Instead of using an action JSON file and a separate prompt file, you can define a sub-agent in a single Markdown file. Place the file in one of the AI action folders configured in the page. The file begins with a YAML front matter block that names the sub-agent and specifies when to use it, followed by the prompt that instructs it.

Example:--- name: Style Reviewer description: Reviews a topic against the documentation style guide and reports what should be changed. Use it before a topic is published. tools: get_document_content, grep_project, search_project_resources ---
You are a documentation reviewer.
Read the topic you are given and check it against the style guide of the project. Report what should be changed and why. Do not edit the document yourself.

A sub-agent defined this way does not appear in the Chat modes drop-down menu. Instead, it is available to AI agents that delegate work. These agents discover the sub-agent from its description and invoke it by using the invoke_ai_agent tool. The sub-agent ID is computed from its name (for example, agent.style-reviewer for the preceding sub-agent). If two definitions produce the same ID, only the first is loaded, and the others are reported in the application log.

The YAML front matter may contain the following keys:
name (Required) The name of the sub-agent, presented to the AI agent that invokes it and used to compute its ID.
description (Required) Describes when to invoke this sub-agent. An AI agent reads this description when choosing from the available sub-agents, so describe the sub-agent's purpose rather than how it works.
tools
(Optional) Specifies the tools that the sub-agent may call. List the tools either on one line, separated by commas, or as a YAML list. If this key is missing, the sub-agent inherits the tools of the built-in Agent chat mode, except for tools that invoke agents. This prevents a sub-agent from delegating to itself. Declaring the key without specifying a tool gives the sub-agent no tools. A sub-agent that does not declare the key also gets the tools contributed by other plugins and add-ons, while one that declares it gets only the tools it lists.
model (Optional) The ID of the model the sub-agent runs with. By default, it runs with the model used by the conversation that invoked it.
visibility (Optional) Accepts the same values as the visibility property of an AI action. The default value for a sub-agent is visible-only-for-tools. Set it to visible to also show the sub-agent in the Chat modes drop-down menu.
output-action (Optional) Takes the same values as the output-action property of an AI action. The default is agentic, which is what makes the file define a sub-agent rather than an ordinary action.
profile (Optional) Restricts the sub-agent to certain applications, with the same values as the profile property of an AI action.

A Markdown file in the same folders is loaded as a sub-agent only if it contains this type of front matter. A file named SKILL.md is a skill, and a file without front matter is an ordinary prompt referenced by an action through its prompt_ref property.
